title: Efficiently Learning Drifting Halfspaces with Massart Noise

exact_contract_summary.claim_1: For drifting gamma-margin halfspaces with eta-Massart noise, there exists a poly(d,1/gamma,1/Delta)-time algorithm; for any T=Omega_tilde(Delta^(-2/3)), with probability at least 9/10 its error is at most eta+O_tilde(Delta^(1/3)/gamma).
exact_contract_summary.claim_2: For (1/3)-RCN and T >= gamma^(-1/6) Delta^(-2/3), there exists a family of instances such that, conditional on the low-degree hardness conjecture, no polynomial-time algorithm attains error opt_T+Delta^(1/3) gamma^(-1/6) on every instance.
exact_contract_summary.claim_3: For every drifting binary concept process realized by a VC-dimension-d class under eta-Massart noise, for every sufficiently late t=Omega_tilde(d/((1-2eta)Delta)), an algorithm has error at most opt_t+O_tilde(sqrt(d Delta/(1-2eta))) with probability at least 9/10.
exact_contract_summary.claim_4: For every T>0 and Delta in (0,1), there exists a family of eta-RCN halfspace instances such that, when (1-2eta)^3>d Delta, no algorithm attains err_T <= opt_T+o(sqrt(d Delta/(1-2eta))) with probability 1/2 on every instance.
exact_contract_summary.claim_5: For fixed c in (0,1/2), eta=1/3, and Delta>2^(-1/gamma^c), no polynomial of degree less than O(gamma^(-c/4)) is a 1-distinguisher for Definition 4.1 instantiated by Definition 4.3.
exact_contract_summary.claim_6: The paper states sqrt(Delta), not Delta: for T=Omega_tilde((gamma Delta)^(-1/2)), an efficient algorithm has err_T=O_tilde(sqrt(Delta) gamma^(-3/2)) with probability at least 9/10; the compared prior rate is O_tilde(sqrt(Delta) gamma^(-2)).
